newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end higher, paring earlier loss.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end higher, paring earlier loss.

text.p: Singapore shares ended slightly higher on Monday, paring morning losses, thanks to buying by funds in the afternoon, brokers said.

"The shares finished higher in line with some other Asian bourses as fund managers switched their attention to Singapore after buying in Hong Kong and elsewhere," a director at a securities house said.

The key Straits Times Industrials Index was up 6.11 points at 2,177.16 against a low of 2,163.28. Volume was 67.84 million units reflecting a listless trade. The broader market was mixed with losers leading gainers by 162 to 131.
Topping the actives was newly-listed engineering group Presscrete with 5.11 million shares. It ended at S$0.345 ($0.243) against its initial public offer price of S$0.30.

Malayan Bank, Singapore Press Foreign and Creative Technology were among top gainers, rising by between S$0.60 and S$25 cents. Thai Prime Fund 200 headed the gainers, rising US$0.60 to US$16.10 on a rally in Thai stocks, dealers said.
Losers included OUT, Jurong Shipyard, SPK Sentosa Corp and DBS Bank Foreign, falling between S$0.30 and S$1.00.
